summary: Rapid 429s after migration to HTTP/2 multiplexing with aggressive client retry splay
description:
Issue summary:
Customer migrated their ingestion clients to an HTTP/2 multiplexed uploader (single TLS connection, many concurrent streams) and enabled a client-side retry splay library. Within minutes of the migration they observed large numbers of 429 responses from Redwood's hosted API for their dedicated pool. Impact:
- Several customer-critical ingestion pipelines started failing intermittently with 429s, causing downstream indexing delays (~30-60min backlog) and spike in support alerts.
- Affects dedicated pool (DocuStream dedicated shard) during sustained parallel stream start bursts.
Environment:
- DocuStream dedicated pool (tenant: docustream-prod) in us-east-1
- API path: POST /v1/streams/generate (streaming + function-calling enabled)
- Client: custom Go uploader (http2, keepalive, retry-splay lib v0.3.1)
Steps to reproduce (customer-provided):
1) Open a single HTTP/2 TLS connection to api.redwood.example (us-east-1).
2) Start 400 concurrent streams over that connection, each initiating a generation request with ~512 token prompt.
3) Configure client retry splay to immediately attempt up to 3 fast retries on transient network errors.
4) Observe 200-400 429 responses within the first 2 minutes, then periodic bursts as retries re-fire.
Logs / initial observations:
- Edge proxy logs show per-stream rate-accounting increments for the same upstream connection (edge-proxy increments +400 token-meter entries within 30s).
- Rate limiter returned HTTP 429 with x-rate-limit-retry-after: 30s for many requests.
- Dedicated pool metrics show brief token burn followed by autoscaler attempting to add capacity but falling behind due to burst-accounting.
- No corresponding billing/usage spike in customer console (reporting lag) which confused the customer.
Hypothesis:
- Recent edge-proxy change (PR #1428) changed quota accounting from per-connection to per-stream for HTTP/2. For single-connection multiplexed clients, this turned a single client burst into many distinct charge events against the tenant token bucket, effectively amplifying short bursts.
- Client-side retry splay aggressively replays short-lived failures which multiplies the effective request rate during warmup.
- Dedicated pool autoscaler scales on sustained CPU/GPU metrics and cannot react to immediate token-burst spikes; combined with per-stream accounting it caused early throttles (429) before scaling could take effect.
Customer impact and ask:
- Customer requested guidance to avoid repeated 429s while they coordinate a rollback and client throttling changes. They asked for temporary smoothing of quota windows or an emergency increase to burst capacity for docustream-prod.
investigation_notes: 2026-03-10 09:12 UTC - Support intake: Customer reported spike in 429s right after rolling out HTTP/2 uploader. Ticket created.

2026-03-10 09:45 UTC - Pulled edge-proxy release history; identified PR #1428 deployed three hours before incident. PR changes: per-stream accounting fix for HTTP/2 multiplexing (intended to avoid per-connection bypass).

2026-03-10 10:05 UTC - Correlated edge-proxy logs: a single TLS connection showed >380 stream start events within 60s; rate-limiter recorded 380 separate accounting increments against tenant token bucket.

2026-03-10 10:30 UTC - Checked dedicated pool autoscaler logs: scale-up triggered but new nodes not ready before token bucket exhausted; autoscaler uses 3-minute lookback which is too slow for short bursts.

2026-03-11 02:00 UTC - Reproduced locally with a test harness mimicking client: when using HTTP/2 multiplexing plus immediate retry splay, token accounting increased by factor ~Nstreams per connection.
comments: Aisha Patel (Support) 2026-03-10 09:20 UTC: Thanks for the report — we're investigating. Please capture an example request IDs if you can.
Alex Nguyen (SRE) 2026-03-10 09:58 UTC: Noted the timing of edge-proxy deploy. Adding edge-proxy on-call to confirm behavior change. Linking PR #1428 for reference.

DocuStream (Customer) 2026-03-10 10:02 UTC: We can temporarily throttle at the client, but we need an emergency tweak on Redwood side to avoid blocking ingestion. Can you allow a short burst window for docustream-prod?

Tomás Rivera (SRE) 2026-03-10 11:12 UTC: Applied temporary smoothing rule to tenant token bucket (increase short burst allowance by +20% for next 2 hours) to reduce immediate 429s while customer rolls back the client. Monitoring metrics now.
Aisha Patel (Support) 2026-03-11 15:34 UTC: Customer confirmed that after smoothing rule they saw reduced 429s and backlog started draining. Suggested next steps documented below.

Engineering (Edge) 2026-03-12 08:00 UTC: Root cause confirmed: PR #1428 introduced per-stream increments. We will patch the accounting to apply a short de-dup window for streams that start within the same connection and 10s interval. Patch PR: github.com/redwood-inference/edge-proxy/pull/1434
resolution: Mitigation applied: temporary burst smoothing for docustream-prod and customer rolled back client-side retry-splay. Engineering root-cause fix (PR #1434) submitted to add a 10s per-connection de-duplication window for per-stream accounting. Post-fix plan: 1) Ship PR #1434 and monitor in staging, 2) Add autoscaler tuning doc for dedicated pools to clarify scale-up latency vs burst behavior, 3) Create customer-facing KB on best practices for HTTP/2 multiplexed clients and retry-splay parameters. Customer confirmed backlog draining and requested knowledge base entry.
follow_up_tasks: ENG-1434: edge-proxy accounting de-dupe window implementation (owner: Edge team)
OPS-3121: Dedicated-pool autoscaler tuning review (owner: Infra/Autoscaler)
DOC-221: KB article - HTTP/2 multiplexing + retry splay guidance (owner: Developer Experience)
